item.text:
Continued. I ran a bounded randomized fault-injection campaign as the remaining coverage gap.

`TestInvestigationRandomFaultCampaign` uses 20 fixed seeds, randomly drops 20% of initial messages, then triggers recovery from a replica lacking the proposed value:

```
random fault campaign summary: pass=11 skip=0 loss=9 divergence=0
```

The nine losses all ended with NOOP committed on the replicas that had committed values. This corroborates the F1 recovery pattern, but the campaign’s classification is coarse: it does not independently prove that every lost value was fast-chosen. The deterministic chosen-value tests establish that. No mixed-value divergence or new root cause was found.

The report, coverage/limits section, and validation matrix now record the campaign and its limitation.

Current status: 22 findings; five cluster controls pass; 34 epaxos finding tests fail as intended; the randomized fault campaign reports 11 pass/9 NOOP losses/0 mixed divergences; both client failover tests and the dlog nil-logger test fail; `go build ./...` passes; captured implementation files remain byte-identical to `../source`.
